name: Winnipeg
registryBasis: The City of Winnipeg publishes an official “Assessment Parcels” dataset maintained by Assessment and Taxation. Its public property map separately labels current assessment parcels (with roll numbers) and survey-parcel lines, and warns the map is reference-only rather than a land survey. The bounded open-data response verified two complete assessment-parcel MultiPolygons within 100 m of the WUP point using only native GISID plus geometry. This verifies the assessment-parcel GIS layer only; it does not establish legal survey or title identity.
scopeLimits: 32 valid distinct public parcel-reference polygons verified in thirteen bounded 0.001-degree cells around the unchanged WUP settlement locator. Complete bounded paging, all 32 fresh native-ID reads, explicit absence, footprint and source binding passed in 60 requests. Independent metric EPSG:32614 GEOS found all geometries valid and distinct, with no sampled overlaps above 0.01 m² or operation errors. Source-native GISID identifies public assessment ground footprints, distinct from property roll/account identifiers and certified survey/title parcels. Counted Socrata paging verifies publication revision before and after each read; identical rows for one GISID are collapsed only when complete geometry is identical. Only GISID, transport row ID, row revision and geometry are requested. The exact point returned no feature; two saved nearby samples match fresh full geometry unchanged. Citywide completeness, legal title, survey accuracy, currentness and long-term identity continuity remain unverified.
pointBasis: UN WUP 2025 population-weighted settlement centroid; this is not a municipal boundary or a parcel-coverage claim.
remainingUncertainty: Citywide completeness, legal title, currentness, survey accuracy and long-term native GIS identity continuity remain unverified.
nextStep: No runtime qualification was attempted. If more discovery is needed, inspect additional first-party metadata and use only bounded geometry requests with a safe native GIS key.

queries.scope: Find city-local registry/map evidence and inspect whether anonymous parcel geometry can be safely requested.
queries.result: Official City property-map documentation distinguishes current assessment parcels from survey parcel lines and warns it is not survey/legal evidence. The official open-data metadata describes the Assessment Parcels dataset and includes GISID and MultiPolygon geometry alongside roll, address, assessment and property fields. The exact-point query returned zero features; a 100 m circle returned two complete MultiPolygons using only GISID and geometry.
queries.executionMethod: Separate language search; official government portal/service review; no property-specific lookup.
